title: newcowf-1997-world

won.source: The federation's own Tournament Finals Results (8 June 1997): Stone Cold Steve Austin pinned The Giant with a third Stone Cold Stunner at 11:24 to win the vacant title.

note: Retained the title at Triple Threat '97 (29 June 1997), pinning Sting then Bret Hart in a triple-threat match, and again at the Great Canadian Bash (24 August 1997), pinning Bret Hart in a match with the entire Hart family caged at ringside.

won.source: The federation's own Tournament Finals Results (8 June 1997): Ric Flair pinned Ahmed Johnson with the figure-four at 21:37 to win the vacant title.

lost.source: The federation's own Triple Threat '97 results (29 June 1997): Chris Benoit hit a top rope headbutt for the pin at 21:02, becoming the new NEWCOWF TV Champion.

won.source: The federation's own Tournament Finals Results (8 June 1997): the Eliminators (John Kronus and Perry Saturn) pinned Doug Furnas and Philip LaFon at 13:42 to win the vacant title.

lost.source: The federation's own Triple Threat '97 results (29 June 1997): Rob Van Dam pinned Tommy Dreamer, substituting for an injured Perry Saturn alongside champion John Kronus, with a split-legged moonsault at 22:13.

won.source: The federation's own Triple Threat '97 results (29 June 1997): Chris Benoit hit a top rope headbutt on Ric Flair for the pin at 21:02 to become the new NEWCOWF TV Champion.

lost.source: The federation's own Clash in the Champions House results (13 July 1997): Ken Shamrock pinned Chris Benoit with a belly-to-belly suplex at 29:58 to win the title.

won.source: The federation's own Clash in the Champions House results (13 July 1997): Ken Shamrock pinned Chris Benoit with a belly-to-belly suplex at 29:58 to win the title.

lost.source: No result documenting this reign's end survives in the held record. The federation's own Halls of Illusions 97 card (billed for 27 July 1997) already rematched Shamrock defending against Chris Benoit, but the operator's own next post says that card's results were never successfully posted; the promotion's own next surviving card, its Great Canadian Bash vote post (10 August 1997), already bills Chris Benoit as TV Champion.

title: newcowf-1997-tv

won.source: The promotion's own billing on its Great Canadian Bash vote card (10 August 1997), 'Chris Benoit(C) vs. Owen Hart', the first surviving document to bill him champion again after losing the title to Ken Shamrock on 13 July 1997; no result documenting the title's return survives in the held record.

source: the federation's own Great Canadian Bash results (25 August 1997), Hockeytown Heaven 97 vote card (25 August 1997) and Halloween Hangover 97 vote card (12 October 1997), all served or cited at newcowf-1997/archive/

title: newcowf-1997-tag-team

won.source: The federation's own Triple Threat '97 results (29 June 1997): Rob Van Dam pinned Tommy Dreamer (substituting for an injured Perry Saturn alongside champion John Kronus) with a split-legged moonsault at 22:13.

lost.source: The federation's own Great Canadian Bash short results (posted 25 August 1997): a four-way title match among Sabu & Rob Van Dam, the Insane Clown Posse, Harlem Heat and the Sandman & Tommy Dreamer ended in a double-pin draw between Harlem Heat and Sabu & Van Dam at 24:37, and the titles were held up.

note: Retained the title at Clash in the Champions House (13 July 1997), Sabu pinning Booker T of Harlem Heat with a moonsault at 29:17 after Insane Clown Posse interference.

won.source: The promotion's own billing on its Halloween Hangover 97 card (12 October 1997), 'Sabu & Rob Van Dam (C) vs. Bret & Owen Hart'. The title had been held up since the Great Canadian Bash four-way draw (24 August 1997) and was still billed as held up, contested against Harlem Heat, on the fed's own Hockeytown Heaven 97 vote card (25 August 1997, for a 28 September 1997 event whose results do not survive in the held record); no result documenting how the hold-up resolved survives.
